note: Every universal this deck prints, and the set it ranges over. A quantifier is a claim about a set, so the set is named the same way a numeral names its computation.

quantifiers.phrase: A Texas city or county is the decider on all thirteen
quantifiers.set: the thirteen items a1 counts. This is clause ONE of the membership test, that the decider type is city or county, so it is true by construction. The set line used to end 'over a data centre or a large load' and call that the whole membership test. The test never computes a relation between the two words it finds, compute.py's own RELATION guard now refuses that wording, and round six found the refuted sentence still standing HERE after it had been taken off the frame. A verification ledger describing a deck that did not ship is worse than no ledger.

quantifiers.about: the two documents this deck reads
quantifiers.set: the two announcements of August 19th 2026, Amazon's own release carried at c1 to c6 and the Office of the Texas Governor's release carried at c7 to c10. Both were re-fetched on August 27th and neither states a local agreement, an abatement, or a public body that acted.

quantifiers.phrase: Thirteen items on this record name a Texas city or county as the decider
quantifiers.set: the same thirteen, and this is clause ONE of the membership test. The caption used to say these thirteen 'do name one', pointing back at 'an acting public body' in its own first paragraph, and round four refuted it on tx-2026-0087, whose record states the council's published record carries no final action. Naming a DECIDER is what the test computes. Naming a body that ACTED is not.

quantifiers.about: the two open proceedings this frame carries
quantifiers.set: the two proceedings on this frame, the Senate committee sittings at c20, c21 and c24 and the PUCT comment window at c22 and c23. Neither the committee's charge nor the Texas Register notice names Amazon or this Austin siting, and the frame says so because both reader rounds found a deck that spends eight frames on one siting and closes on two proceedings about something else with no bridge.

quantifiers.phrase: Each record names a data center or a large load beside a tax break, a moratorium or an incentive
quantifiers.set: the same thirteen items. This is the membership test read out with NO relation between its two halves, which is all the test computes: the item's record names a subject word somewhere and an ask word somewhere. compute.py emits ask_evidence per member so which field each was found in is auditable, and 10 of the 13 carry both words in one sentence.
